outcome.rationale: Primary correlation endpoint likely to show positive association given FEOBV validity in DS and cholinergic-basal forebrain anatomical relationship. Secondary EEG endpoint more uncertain due to limited prior evidence. Single-group design limits generalizability but sufficient for proof-of-concept. Small sample size (n=30) adequate for correlation analysis.

value.uncertainty: No direct published correlation coefficient for this specific endpoint; extrapolated from general cholinergic imaging studies and FEOBV validity in DS
value.rationale: Evidence from PMC11972980 confirms FEOBV PET validity in DS and shows cholinergic associations with cognition and amyloid. Basal forebrain cholinergic volume is anatomically correlated with cholinergic terminal density measured by FEOBV. Prior FEOBV studies in AD (PMC9028526) demonstrate correlations with basal forebrain volumetry. Moderate-to-strong positive correlation expected.

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT05231798 is a Phase 2 single-group study assessing cholinergic integrity in adults with Down syndrome using [18F]-FEOBV PET imaging. Expected completion April 2027.
analysis_trace.indication: Down syndrome with focus on cholinergic system integrity and aging/AD pathology.
analysis_trace.patient_population: Adults aged 18-55 with Down syndrome, non-demented, mental age ≥4 years, n=30 estimated.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: [18F]-FEOBV binds vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT) to quantify cholinergic terminal density. Evidence from PMC11972980 shows DS adults have higher FEOBV uptake than controls but lower uptake with elevated amyloid. Evidence from PMC9028526 shows age-related VAChT binding declines in healthy adults.
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary endpoint: correlation between FEOBV SUVR and basal forebrain cholinergic volume. Secondary: correlation between EEG resting state power and FEOBV SUVR. Both are correlation-based endpoints requiring statistical significance testing.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: FEOBV PET is diagnostic imaging with established safety profile. Radiation exposure is minimal. No therapeutic intervention.
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Single-group design without control limits causal inference. 2) Correlation endpoints may be confounded by age/amyloid. 3) Small sample (n=30) limits statistical power. 4) EEG correlation is exploratory with limited prior evidence in DS.
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Direct evidence from PMC11972980 (Russell et al 2025) shows FEOBV PET is valid in DS adults and correlates with cognition and amyloid. PMC9028526 provides mechanistic support for cholinergic aging effects. No direct evidence for basal forebrain volume correlation or EEG correlation specifically.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No retrieved evidence specifically reporting the correlation coefficient between FEOBV SUVR and basal forebrain volume in DS. No retrieved evidence for EEG resting state power correlation with FEOBV in DS. Expected completion 2027 means results not yet available.
